answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work gating resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent vertex in an interaction graph to solve a key-bound puzzle from a fresh randomness beacon. Enforcing a strict response delta prevents a host from time-slicing one memory bus across concurrent identities, forcing attackers to commit dedicated DRAM bandwidth and energy per identity. During a compute price nadir, however, wealthy adversaries or botnets can still rent burst capacity to register multiple identities.
